topics.title: Overview
topics.summary: A complete agentic chat on Atoms: streaming answers, history, human-in-the-loop decisions, tool activity, tables, charts and your own cards, against any backend on the Neoflo chat standard.
topics.body:
`@neofloai/atoms/chat` is a React chat UI for agentic assistants. Point it at any backend that implements the **Neoflo chat standard** (schema v1, revision 1.3). You get streaming answers, chat history, human-in-the-loop decisions, tool activity, tables, charts and custom cards without building any of it yourself. It's part of Atoms and built from Atoms components and tokens, so it looks like the rest of your Neoflo product in light and dark. ## What you get - **A complete chat in one component.** `` renders the history panel, the thread and the composer. - **An empty chat that invites the first question.** The greeting, the composer and the backend's suggested prompts sit in one column, each prompt with its icon. A prompt the user removes stays removed on that device. - **Streaming that holds up in production.** It handles SSE over `fetch`, snapshot-based deltas, cancel, retry, idle timeouts and dropped connections. - **Human-in-the-loop.** Approval and choice cards pause the turn, lock the composer, and resume with your decision. - **12 built-in blocks.** Text, thinking, tool call, table, sources, approval, choice, error, artifact, image, plan and charts. - **Your own cards.** `defineBlock` registers a card, and `actions.emit` routes clicks into your app. - **Chat history.** Search, date groups, rename, archive and delete, all with optimistic updates. - **Configurable local persistence.** Choose session, local, memory, off, or your own storage, partitioned per user. - **Three levels of control.** Use the styled UI, swap parts through slots, or go fully headless with hooks and primitives. - **One standard for every product.** Each backend describes itself through `GET /v1/chat/config`, so the same UI hides what a product doesn't support. A [conformance check](/chat/conformance) tells a backend team what's left to fix. ## Install The chat ships inside Atoms, which installs straight from GitHub. It has no registry, needs no token, and follows semver through release tags: ```bash npm install github:neofloai/atoms#semver:^4.3.0 # The chat's own dependencies — install them in the app that renders a chat npm install react-markdown remark-gfm @radix-ui/react-slot # Only if you use the chart blocks npm install recharts ``` These are optional peer dependencies of Atoms, so an app without a chat never installs them, and an app without charts never installs Recharts. Requirements: - React 18.2 or 19. - A `git` binary on machines that install it. `node:*-alpine` and `-slim` images don't ship one (`apk add --no-cache git`). - Atoms builds itself on install, so don't run `npm ci --ignore-scripts`. ## Entry points | Import | What it contains | Needs | | --- | --- | --- | | `@neofloai/atoms/chat` | ``, every UI part and block, the kit, and the headless engine: runtime, adapters, hooks, primitives, block registry and parsers | `react-markdown`, `remark-gfm`, `@radix-ui/react-slot` | | `@neofloai/atoms/chat/core` | The framework-free engine and the standard's types — no React, so server code can import it | nothing | | `@neofloai/atoms/chat/charts` | `chartBlock` (bar, line, area, donut) and the chart kit | `recharts` | | `@neofloai/atoms/chat/mock` | An in-memory backend on the standard, with demo scenarios — no React | nothing | | `@neofloai/atoms/chat/conformance` | The [backend conformance check](/chat/conformance), also the `atoms-chat-conformance` command — no React | nothing | ## Quick start Mount `NeofloThemeProvider` once, give the chat a sized container, and hand it an adapter: ```tsx import { NeofloThemeProvider } from '@neofloai/atoms'; import { AgenticChat, createRestAdapter } from '@neofloai/atoms/chat'; import { chartBlock } from '@neofloai/atoms/chat/charts'; // getAccessToken stands for your app's own token getter. const adapter = createRestAdapter({ baseUrl: 'https://api.example.com', headers: async () => ({ Authorization: `Bearer ${await getAccessToken()}` }), }); export function App() { return (
); } ``` That's the whole integration. The chat creates a conversation, shows the server's greeting and suggested prompts, streams answers, and keeps history. ## How it talks to your backend `createRestAdapter` implements the endpoints of the chat standard: | # | Call | Used for | | --- | --- | --- | | 0 | `GET /v1/chat/config` | What the backend supports: features, models, sources, limits. | | 1 | `POST /v1/conversation` | New chat. The response supplies the greeting and suggested prompts. | | 2 | `GET /v1/conversations` | The history panel | | 3 | `GET /v1/conversations/{id}` | Opening a chat and its messages | | 4 | `PATCH /v1/conversations/{id}` | Rename, archive, model, default sources | | 5 | `DELETE /v1/conversations/{id}` | Delete | | 6 | `POST /v1/conversations/{id}/messages` | Sending a turn, or resuming a HITL checkpoint. Streamed as SSE. | | 7 | `POST /v1/conversations/{id}/messages/cancel` | The Stop button | It reads all nine stream events (`message_start` through `error`), treats `snapshot` as a full overwrite, and ignores event types it doesn't know. A newer backend therefore never breaks an older UI. Identity comes only from your `headers` or the session cookie. The chat never puts user or tenant data in a payload, and never keeps a credential it was handed. - **The config decides what shows.** The attach button, the scope picker, Archive and approval cards appear only when the backend's `capabilities` allow them. Model and source labels, the workflow catalog and the message length limit come from the config too. A backend without the endpoint (404) gets the defaults, or whatever you pass as `capabilities`. - **Every message has a `client_message_id`.** A retry of a message the server never confirmed reuses it, so a flaky network or a double click never starts two replies. If the server already has it (409 `duplicate_message`), the chat reloads the conversation instead of showing an error. - **Errors are read by code first.** `session_busy`, `rate_limited` (with a countdown), `connection_expired` (with Reconnect) and the rest each get the right action; a code the chat doesn't know falls back to its HTTP status. Each error keeps the server's `request_id` for bug reports. - **Stop matches the backend.** With `cancel: "disconnect"` it closes the stream at once; with `"server"` it calls endpoint 7 first. ## Server rendering The chat is plain React and works in any React app. If yours renders on the server: - Nothing touches `window` or storage at import time or during server render. Persistence hydrates on the client. - `@neofloai/atoms/chat/core`, `@neofloai/atoms/chat/mock` and `@neofloai/atoms/chat/conformance` contain no React, so server code (a route handler, a server action) can import them. - Create the adapter and render `` from a client component — in the Next.js App Router, a file that starts with `'use client'`. An adapter holds functions, and functions can't be passed as props from a server component. ## Where to go next - [Configuration](/chat/configuration): every option of `` and the REST adapter, driving the chat from your app, and adapting a backend that doesn't follow the standard. - [Blocks](/chat/blocks): the built-in blocks an answer is made of. - [Custom blocks](/chat/custom-blocks): your own cards with `defineBlock`. - [Customizing the UI](/chat/customizing): slots, your own layout, composer controls and copy. - [History and persistence](/chat/persistence): the history panel and what the chat remembers on the device. - [Human-in-the-loop](/chat/hitl): approval and choice cards, and decision cards of your own. - [Headless](/chat/headless): the provider, primitives, hooks and parsers with no styling. - [Mock backend](/chat/mock): an in-memory backend for building UI, tests and demos. - [Troubleshooting](/chat/troubleshooting): symptoms and their fixes. - [Backend contract](/chat/backend-contract): the reference for backend teams — auth and credentials, the config, error codes, ordering rules and retries. - [Block contracts](/chat/block-contracts): the payload of every block type. - [Checking a backend](/chat/conformance): the conformance check, for CI. - [Schema gaps](/chat/schema-gaps): what the standard still leaves open.

topics.title: Blocks
topics.summary: The built-in blocks an answer is made of — text, thinking, tool calls, tables, sources, approvals, choices, errors, files, images, plans and charts — and how a block finds its renderer.
topics.body:
A block is one piece of an answer. The renderer is picked by the block's `type`, falling back to its `category`. A product's own `<product>.<name>` type never falls back by category: without a registered renderer it shows its `fallback_text`.

## Built-in blocks

| `type` (aliases) | Renders | Payload |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `text` (`markdown`) | Markdown on the Atoms type scale. Raw HTML is never rendered. | [text](/chat/block-contracts#text) |
| `thinking` (`reasoning`) | "Thought for N seconds". Open while streaming, folds when done. | [thinking](/chat/block-contracts#thinking) |
| `tool_use` + `tool_result` | One card per tool call: name and duration, folded; open it for inputs and results. "Interrupted" when the result never came. | [tool_use](/chat/block-contracts#tool-use-and-tool-result) |
| `tool_call` (`tool`) | The older single-block form of the same card | [tool_call](/chat/block-contracts#tool-call) |
| `table` | A titled, sortable result set with a row count | [table](/chat/block-contracts#table) |
| `sources` (`citations`) | What the answer read. Items can link out or be selectable. | [sources](/chat/block-contracts#sources) |
| `approval` | Approve or reject a proposed action (HITL) | [approval](/chat/block-contracts#approval) |
| `choice` | Single or multi-select question (HITL) | [choice](/chat/block-contracts#choice) |
| `error` | Failure with a Try again button that respects `retry_after` | [error](/chat/block-contracts#error) |
| `artifact` (`document`) | A generated file with a preview, full view and download | [artifact](/chat/block-contracts#artifact) |
| `image` | An image with a caption that opens larger | [image](/chat/block-contracts#image) |
| `plan` (`steps`) | The agent's steps as a live stepper | [plan](/chat/block-contracts#plan) |
| `chart` | Bar, line, area and donut in Atoms colors (`@neofloai/atoms/chat/charts`) | [chart](/chat/block-contracts#chart) |

Charts need `recharts` installed and come from `@neofloai/atoms/chat/charts`: pass its `chartBlock` in `blocks`, as the [quick start](/chat/overview#quick-start) does.

To render a block type of your own, or to replace one of these, see [custom blocks](/chat/custom-blocks).

topics.title: History and persistence
topics.summary: The history panel, and what the chat remembers on the device: where it is stored, what is kept, and clearing it on logout.
topics.body:
The history panel lists the conversations the server keeps. Local persistence remembers state on the device, and you choose where and how much.

## Chat history

The history panel lists conversations from endpoint 2 (`GET /v1/conversations`), newest first. It groups them into Today, Yesterday, Previous 7 days, Previous 30 days and Older, and searches titles as you type. Rename, archive and delete are optimistic, and they roll back if the server refuses.

- A new chat joins the list when its first message is sent. Empty chats never clutter history.
- A reply keeps streaming if you switch chats mid-answer. The list marks that conversation "Replying…".
- `message_stop.title` updates the title everywhere as soon as the server names the chat.
- Build your own panel with `useConversations()`, which returns items, groups, the active id, search, create, select, rename, remove, archive and refresh.

## Local persistence

The chat can remember state on the device, so a reload lands people back where they were: same chat, same half-typed question. You choose where it's stored and what's kept.

```ts
persistence: {
  storage: 'session',          // 'session' (default) | 'local' | 'memory' | 'none' | StorageAdapter
  namespace: 'neoflo-chat',    // key prefix
  scope: user.idHash,          // partitions keys per user
  persist: {
    activeConversation: true,  // reopen the same chat after a reload (not an empty one: see below)
    drafts: true,              // unsent text + uploaded attachments, per chat
    preferences: true,         // history panel, model, scope selection, removed prompts, anything set with usePreference
    history: false,            // conversation list + recent message histories, for instant loads
  },
  maxCachedConversations: 20,  // LRU cap for cached histories
  ttl: undefined,              // ms; older entries are dropped on read
  debounceMs: 400,
}
```

An empty chat isn't reopened. A reload opens a new chat instead, with the server's greeting and suggested prompts, which a reopened one wouldn't have. It is reopened once it has a message, or a half-typed question with `drafts` on.

`history` is off by default because chat content can be sensitive. Turn it on together with `scope`.

Pass `persistence={false}` to turn it off entirely.

## Choosing a storage

| Storage | Survives | Use it when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `session` | Reloads in the same tab | The default. Nothing lingers after the tab closes. |
| `local` | Browser restarts, and it syncs across tabs | People expect the chat to still be there tomorrow. Set `scope`. |
| `memory` | Nothing | Tests and demos. |
| `none` | Nothing | You manage state elsewhere. |
| A `StorageAdapter` | Whatever it does | IndexedDB, localforage, encryption at rest, a native bridge. |

A custom `StorageAdapter`:

```ts
import { createChatRuntime, createRestAdapter, type StorageAdapter } from '@neofloai/atoms/chat/core';

// kv stands for your own async key-value store (IndexedDB, an encrypted store…).

const encryptedStore: StorageAdapter = {
  getItem: async (key) => (await kv.get(key)) ?? null,
  setItem: (key, value) => kv.set(key, value),
  removeItem: (key) => kv.del(key),
  keys: () => kv.keys(), // optional; lets clear() find every key
};

export const runtime = createChatRuntime({
  adapter: createRestAdapter({ baseUrl: 'https://api.example.com' }),
  persistence: {
    storage: encryptedStore,
    scope: 'user-7f3a', // a hash of the signed-in user, so accounts never share state
    persist: { drafts: true, activeConversation: true, preferences: true, history: true },
    maxCachedConversations: 50,
    ttl: 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000, // forget cached chats after a week
  },
});
```

Async adapters are fine. The chat hydrates as soon as reads resolve; sync storages hydrate before the first paint.

## Guarantees

- **Scoped.** Keys are `namespace:scope:name`. Two users on one device never read each other's drafts or history.
- **Versioned.** Every entry is an envelope `{ v, savedAt, data }`. Entries from a newer library version are left alone. Corrupt or foreign entries are deleted instead of crashing the chat.
- **Safe on failure.** A full quota, private mode or a blocked storage falls back to memory for the session and reports once through `onWarning` (`storage_error`).
- **Consistent.** Only finished messages are cached. A message that was mid-stream at reload is shown as interrupted, and the conversation is refetched.
- **Server wins.** Cached history renders instantly and is replaced by the server's copy when it arrives. Decisions made in the session are kept if the server's copy doesn't carry them yet ([schema gap #2](/chat/schema-gaps)).
- **SSR-safe.** Nothing touches storage during server render or at import time.

## Logout

Call `runtime.persistence.clear()` on logout:

```ts
await runtime.persistence.clear(); // removes every key this chat wrote for the current scope
runtime.dispose();
```

When you render `<AgenticChat adapter={…}>` without your own runtime, read it with `useChatRuntime()` inside the tree, or create the runtime yourself with `createChatRuntime` and pass `runtime={…}` (see [driving the chat from your app](/chat/configuration#driving-the-chat-from-your-app)).

topics.title: Headless
topics.summary: The engine and its React bindings with no styling — provider, primitives, hooks and parsers — for a layout the styled components cannot express.
topics.body:
The hooks, primitives and parsers come from the same `@neofloai/atoms/chat` entry as ``. They carry no styling, and when you don't import the styled UI, it tree-shakes away. Use them when a product has its own design system, or when you need a layout the styled components can't express. `@neofloai/atoms/chat/core` goes one step further and has no React at all. ## Example ```tsx import { Block, ChatProvider, Composer, Message, Thread, defineBlock, parseText, useMessage, type ChatAdapter, } from '@neofloai/atoms/chat'; // Headless blocks bring their own renderer; the parsers are shared with the styled UI. const text = defineBlock({ type: 'text', category: 'content', parse: parseText, render: ({ data }) =>

{data.text}

}); function AnyMessage() { const { message } = useMessage(); return ( {/* A tool_result paired with its tool_use renders inside that card (Message.Blocks does this for you). */} {message.blocks .filter((b) => !b.pairedWith) .map((b) => ( ))} ); } export function MyChat({ adapter }: { adapter: ChatAdapter }) { return (

Ask me anything.

 {(label) => {label}} ↓ Stop Send ); } ``` ## Provider ```tsx import { ChatProvider } from '@neofloai/atoms/chat'; … ``` `ChatProvider` takes every runtime option (see [Configuration](/chat/configuration#options)), or a `runtime` you created with `createChatRuntime`. `ThreadProvider conversationId="…"` pins everything below it to one conversation instead of the active one, which is how you show two chats side by side. ## Primitives Every part renders a plain element, accepts normal HTML props, supports `asChild` to render your own element instead, and exposes `data-*` attributes (`data-role`, `data-status`, `data-busy`, `data-at-bottom`…) for styling. | Primitive | Parts | | --- | --- | | `Thread` | `Root`, `Viewport` (stick-to-bottom scrolling), `Messages`, `Empty`, `If`, `Status`, `ScrollToBottom` | | `Message` | `Root`, `Blocks` (renders through the registry, with optional grouping), `If` | | `Block` | Renders one block through the registry inside its own error boundary | | `Composer` | `Root` (the form), `Input` (auto-growing, Enter sends, IME-safe, paste files), `Send`, `Cancel`, `AttachmentInput`, `Attachments` | | `Suggestions` | `Root`, `Item` (sends the prompt text). `suggestionGlyph(prompt.icon)` gives the icon a prompt names, or the default. | | `ConversationList` | `Root`, `Item`, `New` | | `Hitl` | `Root`, `Option`, `Submit`, for building choice cards | ## Hooks | Hook | Returns | | --- | --- | | `useThread(selector)` | Any slice of the thread state, re-rendering only when it changes | | `useMessages()`, `useRun()`, `useThreadMeta()`, `useIsBusy()` | Common slices | | `useComposer()` | Draft text, attachments, `canSend`, `busy`, `blockedByDecision`, `send`, `cancel`, `addFiles` | | `useConversations()` | History: items, groups, search, create, select, rename, remove, archive | | `useScope()` | The workflow picker: groups, selection, summary, `toggle`, `setGroup` | | `useHitl()` | The current block's checkpoint state and `submit` | | `useChatActions()` | `send`, `resume`, `cancel`, `retry`, conversation actions, `emit` | | `useChatConfig()`, `useCapabilities()` | The backend's config (`models`, `sources` and the rest), and the capabilities the UI may use | | `usePreference(key, fallback)` | A persisted UI preference | | `useChatEvent(type, listener)` | Runtime events: `event`, `error`, `warning`, `activeChange` | | `useChatRuntime()` | The runtime itself | ## Parsers Every built-in block's parser is exported (`parseTable`, `parseToolCall`, `parseApproval`, …) along with `BLOCK_TYPES`, so a headless renderer can reuse the exact payload handling of the styled UI: ```tsx import { BLOCK_TYPES, defineBlock, parseTable } from '@neofloai/atoms/chat'; const table = defineBlock({ type: BLOCK_TYPES.table, parse: parseTable, render: MyTable }); ```

topics.title: Troubleshooting
topics.summary: Symptoms and their fixes: a chat with no height, the wrong theme, unsupported content, cards that do nothing, a 401 loop, missing controls.
topics.body:
Find the symptom in the left column; the fix is beside it.

| Symptom | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| `Cannot find module ./dist/index.mjs` from Atoms | Your install skipped scripts. Remove `--ignore-scripts`. |
| `git: not found` in CI or Docker | Install git in the image: `apk add --no-cache git`. |
| The chat has no height, or never scrolls | Give its container a height (`height: 100vh`, or a flex child with `min-height: 0`). |
| Wrong fonts or colors, plus a console warning about `NeofloThemeProvider` | Mount `NeofloThemeProvider` once at the root. |
| An "Unsupported content: …" box | The backend sent a block type nothing renders. Register a `defineBlock` for it ([custom blocks](/chat/custom-blocks)). The box only shows in development. |
| Cards do nothing when clicked | Handle `onAction`. Cards emit, and your app decides. |
| A 401 loop | Return `false` from `onUnauthorized` when the refresh fails. The error then surfaces instead of retrying. |
| No attach button, scope picker, Archive or approval cards | The backend's config turns them off. Check `useCapabilities()`, or the config endpoint's `capabilities`. |
| A connection error with no Reconnect button | Pass `onConnectionRequired`. Without it the chat can only show the message. |
| A tool card says "Interrupted" | The reply ended without that tool's `tool_result`. Every `tool_use` needs exactly one, including on error. |

topics.title: Backend contract
topics.summary: For backend teams: the endpoints, the auth and identity rules, the config, the event stream, errors, cancel and retries the chat expects.
topics.body:
This page is for teams building a backend that the Atoms chat (`@neofloai/atoms/chat`) talks to. It restates the Neoflo chat standard (schema v1, revision 1.3) from the client's side: what the chat sends, what it expects back, and how it behaves when something goes wrong. Ask Neo is the first product on it; any other product implements the same endpoints and adds its own values through the config and `ext`.

Block payloads (what goes inside `content_block_*`) live in [block contracts](/chat/block-contracts). What the standard still leaves open is in [schema gaps](/chat/schema-gaps). To check a backend against this page, run the [conformance check](/chat/conformance).

## 1. Rules for every endpoint

### Auth, identity and credentials

- **Login** is a Bearer header or a session cookie, chosen per product. The client sends whatever `headers` the host app configures, or the cookie with `credentials: 'include'`.
- **Who the user is** (user, workspace, tenant) comes only from the session. No request or response body carries `user_id`, `workspace_id`, `tenant_id` or `object`.
- **Credentials for other systems** (an ERP, Zoho, Freshdesk, invoice processing) live only on the server, as a workspace connection. They never appear in chat requests or responses.
- **The browser only sees a connection's status:** a source's `meta.connection` is `{ "status": "connected" | "expired" | "missing", "expires_at": "…" | null }` and nothing else.
- A missing or expired connection returns 422 `connection_required` or `connection_expired` with `details.source`, before the stream opens. If it expires mid-reply, send a stream `error` with the same code.
- Cookies are `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax` (or `None` when cross-site). POST, PATCH and DELETE check `Origin` or a CSRF token. CORS allows credentials only for listed origins, never `*`.

### Errors

Every non-2xx response uses one envelope, and HTTP errors and stream `error` events share one list of codes:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "connection_expired",
    "message": "Reconnect invoice processing to continue.",
    "retry_after": null,
    "request_id": "req_01HZX4",
    "details": { "source": "invoice_processing" }
  }
}
```

`message` is shown to the user. `request_id` is also sent as the `X-Request-Id` header. A product adds its own codes as `<product>.<code>`. The client reads the code first and falls back to the HTTP status only for codes it doesn't know:

| Code | HTTP | What the client does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `invalid_request` | 422 | Shows the message. |
| `unsupported_feature` | 422 | Shows the message. Turn the feature off in the config so the UI hides it. |
| `connection_required`, `connection_expired` | 422 | Calls the host's `onConnectionRequired(sourceId)`, then retries once; else shows Reconnect. |
| `unauthenticated` | 401 | Calls the host's `onUnauthorized({ code })` once and retries the request if it returns true. |
| `access_denied` | 403 | Shows the message. No retry. |
| `not_found` | 404 | Removes the chat from history. A 404 on DELETE counts as deleted. |
| `session_busy` | 409 | Shows "a reply is already in progress" with Try again. |
| `duplicate_message` | 409 | Reloads the conversation to show the reply the first attempt started. No error is shown. |
| `rate_limited` | 429 | Counts down `retry_after` (or `Retry-After`) before Try again. |
| `upstream_unavailable` | 502, 503 | Offers Try again. |
| `internal` | 500 | Offers Try again. |
| `<product>.<code>` | any | Behaves as its HTTP status. A 401 product code (`askneo.gate_required`) goes to `onUnauthorized`. |

### General

- Paths are `/v1/...` relative to the product's base URL. The client's `paths` option remaps them.
- Ids are opaque strings. Times are ISO-8601 UTC.
- Both sides ignore fields, events and block types they don't know, so either can add things without breaking the other.
- Product-only fields go in `ext.<product id>`, never next to the shared fields.
- Timeouts: REST calls time out after 30 s. A stream has no total limit but counts as dropped after 60 s without any event, so send `: ping` after 15 s of silence.
- Retries: the client retries GET, PATCH, DELETE and cancel up to 2 times on network errors, 5xx and 429. It never retries POST `/conversation` or POST `/messages` automatically.

## 2. Endpoints

| # | Request | The client expects |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | `GET /v1/chat/config` | What this backend supports (section 3). Called once per session. A 404 means "no config": the host's switches apply. |
| 1 | `POST /v1/conversation`, optional body `{ title, model, sources }` | 201 with the conversation object plus `greeting` and `suggested_prompts` (`{ label, prompt, icon? }[]`: the row shows `label` and sends `prompt`, see [Suggested prompts](#suggested-prompts)). |
| 2 | `GET /v1/conversations` | `{ "conversations": [...], "next_cursor": null }`. Items carry `conversation_id`, `title`, `selected_model`, `archived`, `message_count`, timestamps. No `sources`. |
| 3 | `GET /v1/conversations/{id}` | The conversation object plus `messages[]`, oldest first. A 404 removes the chat from history. |
| 4 | `PATCH /v1/conversations/{id}` with `title`, `model`, `sources`, `archived` | The conversation object. The client keeps the `sources` from this response, not the ones it sent. `archived` only with the `archive` capability. |
| 5 | `DELETE /v1/conversations/{id}` | 204. A 404 also counts as success. |
| 6 | `POST /v1/conversations/{id}/messages` | An SSE stream (section 4). |
| 7 | `POST /v1/conversations/{id}/messages/cancel` with `{ "message_id" }` | `{ "status": true \| false }` (section 5). |

The conversation object (endpoints 1, 3, 4):

```json
{
  "conversation_id": "6650f1c2a9b8d3e4f5a6b7c8",
  "title": "New chat",
  "subtitle": "Ask Neo",
  "archived": false,
  "selected_model": "claude-haiku-4-5",
  "sources": [
    { "id": "search_v2", "enabled": true, "meta": { "search_v2_chunk_size": 10 } },
    {
      "id": "invoice_processing",
      "enabled": false,
      "meta": { "connection": { "status": "connected", "expires_at": "2026-10-09T09:00:00Z" } }
    }
  ],
  "message_count": 0,
  "created_at": "2026-10-06T09:12:00Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-10-06T09:12:00Z",
  "ext": { "askneo": {} }
}
```

### Suggested prompts

The prompts under the empty chat's composer come from endpoint 1:

```json
{
  "greeting": "Good morning, Priya!",
  "suggested_prompts": [
    { "label": "What is waiting on me right now?", "prompt": "Which invoices are waiting on me?", "icon": "inbox" },
    { "label": "Which invoices are stuck?", "prompt": "Which invoices are stuck, and why?", "icon": "warning" },
    { "label": "Show last week's spend by vendor", "prompt": "Show last week's spend by vendor as a chart", "icon": "chart" }
  ]
}
```

- **`label`** is what the row shows, and **`prompt`** is what it sends.
- **`icon`** is optional (revision 1.3). It names one of a fixed list, so the chat ships those glyphs and no others: `sparkle`, `inbox`, `warning`, `chart`, `trend`, `document`, `receipt`, `money`, `vendor`, `calendar`, `clock`, `check`, `search`. A prompt without one, or with a name this list doesn't have, shows `sparkle`, so a backend on revision 1.2 needs no change.
- The user can remove a prompt with its ×. The chat remembers that on the device and stops showing that prompt in new chats, so send the ones worth keeping first.

Messages (endpoint 3) carry `message_id`, `role`, `content` (a block array), `stop_reason`, `created_at`, and on assistant messages `run_id`, `model` and optional `usage`. User messages carry the `client_message_id` they were sent with, and the `sources`, `attachments` and `workflow_context` the turn used. `ext` is passed to the host app untouched.

## 3. The config (endpoint 0)

```json
{
  "protocol_version": "1.3",
  "product": { "id": "askneo", "name": "Ask Neo" },
  "capabilities": {
    "hitl": false,
    "attachments": false,
    "workflow_context": false,
    "archive": false,
    "cancel": "disconnect",
    "per_turn_model": true,
    "per_turn_sources": true,
    "conversation_pagination": false,
    "message_pagination": false,
    "stream_resume": false
  },
  "models": [{ "id": "claude-haiku-4-5", "label": "Haiku 4.5", "default": true }],
  "sources": [{ "id": "search_v2", "label": "Knowledge base", "default_enabled": true, "meta": {} }],
  "workflows": [],
  "limits": { "max_message_chars": 100000, "max_attachments": 0, "max_attachment_bytes": 0, "attachment_types": [] }
}
```

A flag missing from a returned config means "not supported". What the client does with it:

| Field | The client |
| --- | --- |
| `hitl: false` | Ignores `checkpoint` events and never shows approval or choice cards. |
| `attachments: false` | Hides the attach button and never sends `attachments`. |
| `workflow_context: false` | Hides the scope picker and never sends `workflow_context`. |
| `archive: false` | Hides Archive and the archived filter. |
| `cancel` | `"disconnect"`: Stop closes the stream at once. `"server"`: Stop calls endpoint 7 first (section 5). |
| `per_turn_model` | Sends the conversation's model as `model` with each message. |
| `per_turn_sources: false` | Sets sources per conversation only (endpoint 4), never per message. |
| `sources` | Labels sources in the UI. The client only sends source ids listed here. |
| `workflows` | Fills the scope picker (one group per workspace) when the host app doesn't pass its own catalog. |
| `limits` | Blocks a message over `max_message_chars`, and applies the attachment limits on top of the host's. |
| `sources[].meta.connection` | A hint only. Connection status comes from the conversation responses and from `connection_*` errors. |

The host app can turn more off with the `capabilities` option, but can't turn on what the config says is unsupported.

## 4. Sending a message (endpoint 6)

```json
{
  "stream": true,
  "client_message_id": "cm_7f3a91",
  "message": { "role": "user", "type": "default", "content": { "default": "What were Acme's top open invoices last quarter?" } },
  "model": "claude-sonnet-5",
  "sources": [{ "id": "search_v2", "enabled": true, "meta": { "search_v2_chunk_size": 5 } }]
}
```

- `client_message_id` is created by the client. A repeat with the same id returns 409 `duplicate_message`. The client reuses the id when it retries a message the server never confirmed (no `message_start` arrived), and sends a new one when it did.
- `model` is sent only with `per_turn_model`. `sources` (settings only, never credentials), `workflow_context`, `attachments` and `ext` are sent only when they have content and the config allows them.
- Inputs the config turns off return 422 `unsupported_feature` before the stream opens. They're never silently ignored.
- Return 409 `session_busy` before the stream opens when a reply is already running in the conversation.

A HITL resume (only with `hitl`) uses exactly the schema shape:

```json
{
  "stream": true,
  "message": { "role": "user", "type": "hitl", "content": { "checkpoint_id": "z93hdnf02c", "decision": "approve" } }
}
```

The response is `text/event-stream`, with `Cache-Control: no-cache` and `X-Accel-Buffering: no`:

```
message_start → (status | content_block_start → content_block_delta* → content_block_stop | checkpoint)* → message_delta? → message_stop
```

| Event | What the client does |
| --- | --- |
| `message_start` | Opens the assistant message, keyed by `message_id`, and keeps the id for cancel. `user_message_id` and the echoed `client_message_id` swap the optimistic user message for the saved one. |
| `status` | Shows `label` in the run-status tag until the next `status` or the end of the turn. |
| `content_block_start` | Adds the block, keyed by `block.id`, so **`id` must be unique within a message**. `index` only has to be unique within one stream. |
| `content_block_delta` | `snapshot` replaces the block's streaming field (or the whole payload when it's an object). Without it, `delta.text` is appended. Send snapshots: they make a dropped delta harmless. |
| `content_block_stop` | Replaces the block with the final `block`, the source of truth. |
| `checkpoint` | With `hitl`: attaches `{ checkpoint_id, requires }` to the block at `block_index` and makes that card actionable. |
| `message_delta` | Stores `usage`, which is optional. |
| `message_stop` | Ends the turn with `stop_reason`. Always send it, including after an error. A non-null `title` renames the chat everywhere. |
| `error` | `error_type` comes from the shared code list. Shows an error card with the action the code calls for (section 1). |
| `: ping` | A comment line, ignored. Send it after 15 s with no event so proxies and the client keep the stream open. |
| `<product>.<event>` | Ignored by clients that don't know it. |

Every `tool_use` gets exactly one `tool_result` (with `tool_use_id`), including on error, and the client shows both as one card. A reply that ends without a tool's result shows that card as "Interrupted". `tool_result.http_trace` is null in production.

Tolerance: an unknown event type is ignored; a malformed event is skipped with a warning; a stream that ends without `message_stop` marks the answer interrupted with Try again; the data's `type` wins over the SSE `event:` name.

## 5. Stop (endpoint 7)

- **`cancel: "server"`**: the client posts `{ "message_id" }` from `message_start`. `true` means the run is stopping; the client waits up to 1.5 s for `message_stop` (`stop_reason: "cancelled"`) and then closes the stream. `false` (the turn already finished, or nothing can stop it) closes the stream at once. If Stop comes before `message_start`, the client waits up to 3 s for it, then closes the stream.
- **`cancel: "disconnect"`**: the client closes the stream at once and never calls endpoint 7. The backend stops the run and saves the partial reply as `cancelled`. The endpoint, if it exists, always returns `{ "status": false }`.

## 6. History and HITL

On reload, endpoint 3 has to let the UI rebuild each card. The client pairs each `tool_result` with its `tool_use` again, and for HITL ([schema gap #2](/chat/schema-gaps)) reads:

- a checkpoint on the HITL block, as `checkpoint: { checkpoint_id, requires, status: "pending" | "resolved", decision }` or a bare `checkpoint_id`;
- a user message with `type: "hitl"` and `content: { checkpoint_id, decision }`, applied to the matching card and not rendered as a bubble;
- a last assistant message with `stop_reason: "paused"` and an unresolved checkpoint, which becomes live again.

## 7. Connections (optional pattern)

A product whose chat uses a third-party system can expose `/v1/connections/{source_id}`: `PUT` (the host app hands over a credential it holds), `GET` (`{ status, expires_at }`) and `DELETE`. The host app calls these, typically from `onConnectionRequired`; the chat never does. Nothing about the credential is returned.

## 8. Conformance check

A conformance check calls a backend the way the UI will and reports every gap against this page. [Checking a backend](/chat/conformance) covers what it checks and how to run it in CI.

topics.title: Block contracts
topics.summary: The payload of every built-in block type with the aliases the parsers accept, and the rules for a product’s own blocks.
topics.body:
This page defines the payload of every block the chat renders out of the box, the standard types every product's backend can send. Every block carries `id`, `type` and `category`. The fields below are the rest.

The parsers accept the aliases and fallbacks listed, so a backend can adopt these shapes gradually. A block the client can't parse falls back to a development-only "unsupported content" notice and never crashes the thread.

**The vocabulary is closed on purpose.** A turn composes these shapes and never invents a layout. A product's own cards use [`<product>.<name>` types](/chat/block-contracts#product-blocks), registered by that product's app with `defineBlock`.

## text

```json
{ "id": "b1", "type": "text", "category": "content", "text": "Four are waiting on you…" }
```

- `text` is Markdown (GFM tables, lists, code). Raw HTML is not rendered. Aliases: `markdown`, `content`.
- Stream it with `snapshot` set to the full text so far.

## thinking

```json
{
  "id": "b2",
  "type": "thinking",
  "category": "reasoning",
  "text": "The price difference is against the order…",
  "duration_ms": 4000
}
```

- `text` (or `thinking`) is the model's reasoning. `duration_ms` is optional; the client measures it while streaming if it's missing.

## tool_use and tool_result

The standard way to show a tool call: a `tool_use` block when the call starts, and exactly one `tool_result` when it returns, including on error. The client pairs them by `tool_use_id` and renders one card: the call's input, then what it returned.

```json
{ "id": "toolu_01A9", "type": "tool_use", "category": "tool", "tool": "search_v2", "input": { "query": "Acme open invoices Q3" } }
```

```json
{
  "id": "f4a5b6c7",
  "type": "tool_result",
  "category": "tool",
  "tool_use_id": "toolu_01A9",
  "is_error": false,
  "error_code": null,
  "result_count": 2,
  "results": [{ "title": "INV-1042", "snippet": "Acme Corp · $12,400 · open", "url": null }],
  "http_trace": null
}
```

| Field | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `tool_use.tool` | The tool id, shown as the title. Aliases: `name`, `tool_name`. |
| `tool_use.title` | Optional friendlier title. |
| `tool_use.input` | Shown as key/value rows. |
| `tool_result.tool_use_id` | The `tool_use` block's `id`. A result with no matching call in the message gets a card of its own. |
| `tool_result.is_error` | `true` shows the card as failed, with `error_code` (or `error`/`message`) as the reason. |
| `tool_result.result_count` | Shown as "N results". Up to five `results` are listed under it, as `{ title, snippet, url }`; `url` becomes a link. |
| `tool_result.http_trace` | Debug data. `null` in production, and never shown. |

Until its result arrives the card shows "Running". If the reply ends (`message_stop` other than `paused`, Stop, or a dropped stream) without the result, the card shows "Interrupted" instead of spinning.

## tool_call

The older single-block form, still accepted: one block carries both the input and the result.

```json
{
  "id": "b3",
  "type": "tool_call",
  "category": "tool",
  "name": "search_invoices",
  "input": { "workspace": "Finance", "status": "held", "window": "30d" },
  "status": "success",
  "result_summary": "4 rows",
  "duration_ms": 800
}
```

| Field | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `name` | The tool id, shown as the title. Aliases: `tool_name`, `tool`. |
| `title` | Optional friendlier title. |
| `input` | Shown as key/value rows. Aliases: `arguments`, `args`, `parameters`. Streaming `partial_json` deltas also work. |
| `status` | `running`, `success` or `error`. |
| `result_summary` | One line shown as `returned`. Without it, `output` is shown compactly. |
| `error` | Shown in red when `status` is `error`. |
| `duration_ms` | Shown as meta ("0.8s"). |

Send `content_block_start` with `status: "running"` and `content_block_stop` with the final status and result.

## table

```json
{
  "id": "b4",
  "type": "table",
  "category": "ui",
  "title": "Held invoices",
  "columns": [
    { "key": "vendor", "label": "Vendor" },
    { "key": "reason", "label": "Reason" },
    { "key": "amount", "label": "Amount", "format": "currency", "currency": "USD" }
  ],
  "rows": [{ "vendor": "Redwood Components", "reason": "Price vs order", "amount": 3940.24 }],
  "total_rows": 4
}
```

- `columns` entries can be plain strings. `format` is one of `text`, `number`, `currency`, `percent` or `date`. Numeric formats right-align.
- `rows` can be objects keyed by column, or arrays in column order.
- `total_rows` is shown as "N rows" when the block carries a preview of a bigger result. The client renders up to 500 rows.

## sources

```json
{
  "id": "b5",
  "type": "sources",
  "category": "citation",
  "items": [
    { "id": "s1", "label": "Invoice Processing · 30 days", "url": "https://…", "description": "…" },
    { "id": "s2", "label": "Purchase orders · Redwood Components", "selected": true }
  ]
}
```

- A `url` opens in a new tab. Every click also reaches the host app as `open_source`.
- If any item has `selected`, the list shows checkboxes. Toggling one emits `source_toggle`.

## approval

A human-in-the-loop yes or no. Pair it with a `checkpoint` event.

```json
{
  "id": "b6",
  "type": "approval",
  "category": "hitl",
  "title": "Post 4 invoices to NetSuite?",
  "description": "They total 10,061.74 across three vendors. Posting cannot be undone from here.",
  "approve_label": "Post all four",
  "reject_label": "Not now",
  "tone": "default",
  "details": { "vendors": 3, "total": "10,061.74" }
}
```

- The decision sent back is `approve_value` / `reject_value`, which default to `"approve"` / `"reject"`.
- `tone: "danger"` colors the approve button for destructive actions. `details` renders as key/value rows.
- An unknown `type` in the `hitl` category also renders as an approval, unless it carries `options`.

## choice

A single- or multi-select question. Pair it with a `checkpoint` event.

```json
{
  "id": "b7",
  "type": "choice",
  "category": "hitl",
  "title": "Which workflows should I review?",
  "multiple": true,
  "min": 1,
  "max": 2,
  "options": [
    { "value": "ip", "label": "Invoice Processing" },
    { "value": "col", "label": "Collections" }
  ],
  "submit_label": "Review"
}
```

- The decision is the chosen `value` (single) or an array of values (multiple).
- `options`, `multiple`, `min` and `max` may come in `checkpoint.requires` instead.

## error

```json
{
  "id": "b8",
  "type": "error",
  "category": "error",
  "title": "NetSuite did not answer",
  "message": "The connection timed out after 30 seconds. Nothing was posted.",
  "retryable": true,
  "retry_after": 10
}
```

- Use this for a failure inside a turn that otherwise completes. For a failure that ends the turn, use the `error` stream event.

## artifact

```json
{
  "id": "b9",
  "type": "artifact",
  "category": "ui",
  "filename": "reconciliation-august.md",
  "format": "markdown",
  "content": "# August reconciliation\n…",
  "url": "https://…"
}
```

- `format` is one of `markdown`, `text`, `json`, `csv` or `code`. It's inferred from the filename when missing.
- Inline `content` shows a preview and a full view, and makes the file downloadable. `url` alone offers a download.

## image

```json
{
  "id": "b10",
  "type": "image",
  "category": "ui",
  "url": "https://…/scan.png",
  "alt": "Scan of Statement-Aug.pdf, page 1",
  "caption": "Scan of Statement-Aug.pdf, page 1"
}
```

- `url` must be `https:`, `blob:`, a relative path, or a `data:image/…` URI. Other schemes are dropped.

## plan

```json
{
  "id": "b11",
  "type": "plan",
  "category": "plan",
  "title": "Reconciling August",
  "steps": [
    { "id": "read", "title": "Read the last thirty days", "status": "done" },
    {
      "id": "match",
      "title": "Match each against its order",
      "status": "running",
      "detail": { "compared": "128 invoices", "matched": "124" }
    },
    { "id": "receipts", "title": "Checking receipts", "status": "pending" }
  ]
}
```

- `status` is one of `pending`, `running`, `done`, `failed` or `skipped`. Common synonyms such as `completed` and `in_progress` are accepted.
- Stream progress with `content_block_delta` carrying `snapshot` set to the full `steps` array, or to `{ "steps": [...] }`.

## chart

```json
{
  "id": "b12",
  "type": "chart",
  "category": "ui",
  "chart_type": "bar",
  "title": "Invoices posted",
  "subtitle": "Last five weeks",
  "x_key": "week",
  "series": [
    { "key": "posted", "label": "Posted" },
    { "key": "held", "label": "Held" }
  ],
  "data": [{ "week": "W1", "posted": 22, "held": 12 }],
  "value_format": "number"
}
```

| Field | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `chart_type` | `bar`, `line`, `area` or `donut` (`pie` is accepted as donut). |
| `x_key` | The category field, which is the slice name for donuts. |
| `series` | Numeric fields to plot. Inferred from the first row when missing. A donut uses the first series. |
| `total` | `{ "value": "128", "label": "invoices" }`, shown in the donut's center. |
| `stacked` | Stack bars or areas. |
| `value_format`, `currency` | Axis and tooltip formatting. |

Colors come from the Atoms palette. Don't send hex colors unless a series genuinely needs a fixed one (`series[].color`).

## Product blocks

A product's own card uses the type `<product>.<name>`, where `<product>` is the config's `product.id` (for example `askneo.invoice_card`). It must carry `fallback_text`:

```json
{
  "id": "b9",
  "type": "askneo.invoice_card",
  "category": "ui",
  "fallback_text": "**INV-1042** · Redwood Components · 3,940.24 · held on a price difference",
  "data": { "number": "INV-1042", "amount": 3940.24 }
}
```

- The product's app registers a renderer with `defineBlock({ type: 'askneo.invoice_card', … })`.
- Any other app shows `fallback_text` as Markdown, so the answer still reads correctly. A `<product>.<name>` block is never given to a built-in renderer by its `category`.

## checkpoint.requires

Proposed shape, describing what the decision must look like:

```json
{ "kind": "approve_reject", "options": ["approve", "reject"] }
{ "kind": "multi_select", "options": [{ "value": "ip", "label": "Invoice Processing" }], "min": 1, "max": 2 }
{ "kind": "form", "schema": { "amount": "number" } }
```

The client passes `requires` to the card as-is. Built-in cards read `options`, `multiple`, `min` and `max` from it when the block itself doesn't carry them.

topics.title: Checking a backend
topics.summary: A check that calls a backend the way the chat will and reports every gap against the standard. Run it in CI against dev or staging.
topics.body:
The conformance check calls a backend the way the chat will and reports every gap against the [backend contract](/chat/backend-contract): missing endpoints, identity fields or credentials in bodies, `model` instead of `selected_model`, a stream that doesn't echo `client_message_id`, tools without exactly one result, error bodies outside the envelope, and more. Run it in CI against a dev or staging deployment.

It ships with Atoms 4.4.0 and later, as the `atoms-chat-conformance` command and the `@neofloai/atoms/chat/conformance` subpath. It runs on the same engine the chat does, so the check and the chat can't disagree about the standard. It needs Node 22 or later and nothing else: no React, no components and no dependencies to install.

## What a run does

It creates one conversation, sends one message (which calls the model) and deletes the conversation.

- Failures break the contract. Warnings are worth fixing but don't fail the run.
- Sending a message calls the model, so pass `--no-messages` (or `sendMessages: false` in code) for a run that mustn't. It skips endpoint 6.
- The exit code is 0 when every check passes (warnings allowed), 1 when one fails and 2 on bad usage. `--help` lists every option.

## From the command line

A backend repo doesn't need Atoms in its own dependencies. `npx` fetches it for the run:

```bash
npx --package=github:neofloai/atoms#semver:^4.4.0 atoms-chat-conformance \
  --base-url https://askneo.dev.example \
  --header "Cookie: session=$SESSION"
```

`CHAT_BASE_URL` and `CHAT_HEADERS` (one header per line) work in place of the flags, which keeps a session out of the CI log. `--json` prints the report as JSON.

## From code

`runConformance` takes what the flags set (`baseUrl`, `headers`, `sendMessages`, `prompt`, `checkUnauthenticated`) plus `paths` for a backend that mounts the endpoints elsewhere, and resolves a `ConformanceReport`: `ok`, the counts and every check. `formatReport` turns the report into the text the command prints.

```ts
import { formatReport, runConformance } from '@neofloai/atoms/chat/conformance';

const report = await runConformance({ baseUrl: process.env.CHAT_BASE_URL!, headers: { Cookie: process.env.SESSION! } });
if (!report.ok) throw new Error(formatReport(report));
```

topics.title: Schema gaps
topics.summary: What revision 1.2 of the chat standard settled, what is still open, and what the chat does about each open point today.
topics.body:
Schema v1 left nine points undefined. Revision 1.2 of the standard (the config endpoint, the error envelope, `selected_model`, `client_message_id` and the connection rules) settles most of them. This page tracks what's settled and what's still open. The client already handles every open point.

## Settled in 1.2

| # | Gap | How 1.2 settles it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | **Block vocabulary.** No `type`/`category` values or payloads. | The standard types in [block contracts](/chat/block-contracts), `tool_use` + `tool_result` pairing, and `<product>.<name>` blocks with `fallback_text`. |
| 4 | **Archiving** wasn't in the PATCH body. | `archived` is a PATCH field, behind the `archive` capability. |
| 5 | **Selected model** wasn't returned, and there was no per-turn model. | `selected_model` on endpoints 1–4, the catalog in the config's `models`, and `model` per message with `per_turn_model`. |
| 6 | **Scope catalog.** Nothing listed workflows; `Source` had no label. | The config's `workflows` and labeled `sources`. |
| 8 | **Error bodies** were unspecified. | One envelope, `{ error: { type, message, retry_after, request_id, details } }`, and one code list for HTTP and the stream. |

## Still open

| # | Gap | What the client does today | Proposal |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2 | **HITL state in history.** Endpoint 3 doesn't say how checkpoints and decisions come back. | Reads `checkpoint` on the block and `type: "hitl"` user messages (see [backend contract §6](/chat/backend-contract#6-history-and-hitl)). Keeps decisions made in the session if a reload lacks them. | Settle it when the first product turns `hitl` on. |
| 3 | **Resume message id.** Does a resume continue the paused `message_id` or start a new one? | Handles both. The same id continues the message; a new id adds one. | Continue the same `message_id`, so one answer stays one message. |
| 7 | **Uploads.** Endpoint 6 takes `attachments[]`, but no endpoint produces them. | The host app provides `attachments.upload(file)`. | Keep uploads with each product's file service, or add a shared presigned-upload endpoint. |
| 9 | **Reconnect.** A dropped stream can't be resumed. | Marks the answer interrupted, offers Try again, and refetches on the next open. A retry that the server already received gets 409 `duplicate_message`, and the client reloads the conversation. | Optional endpoint 9, `GET /v1/runs/{run_id}/events`, behind `stream_resume`. |
| 10 | **`stream: false` replies** are still unspecified. | Always streams. Converts a JSON reply if one arrives. | Drop `stream: false` from the standard, or specify it. |
| 11 | **Stop and running tools.** It isn't confirmed whether closing the stream also stops a tool mid-call. | Shows the reply as stopped and any unanswered tool as "Interrupted". | Backends cancel in-flight tool calls when the run stops. |
